source.title: Bayesian filtering unifies adaptive and non-adaptive neural network optimization methods

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; minor typographical errors do not prevent reading.
record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out performance of adaptive optimizers with SGD using benchmark test error and loss, a conceptual test of V4.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-error and test-loss comparisons for optimizers on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. Cited comparisons from prior work are not extracted. Training-curve figures show additional values, but their exact numbers are not stated in the text.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam and SGD using held-out classification error and loss on image benchmarks, testing V4 with the same basic method and measures as its original optimizer comparisons. It is not an original source of V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the conclusion. More precisely, the authors report that their methods are competitive with other adaptive optimizers and sometimes outperform them, while SGD frequently performs better than all adaptive methods, especially on CIFAR-100 test loss. They explicitly caution that these optimizer comparisons justify only limited conclusions.
record.recipe_differences: Uses optimizer comparisons with test-error evaluation, adapting the protocols and optimized hyperparameters from Luo et al. (2019); the paper's main contribution is a new Bayesian filtering optimizer.
record.method_sensitivity: The relative optimizer performance varies by dataset: AdaBayes beats SGD on CIFAR-10 but is slightly worse on CIFAR-100 in the tabulated test errors.
record.problems: The reported experiments cover only CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with two architectures. No uncertainty estimates are stated. The authors caution that only two conclusions can reasonably be drawn. Additional training curves are figures without exact numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 also reports test loss for the optimizers and test error for other optimizers; these were left out to prioritize the direct Adam, SGD and AdaBayes test-error comparison. Figure 4 and Appendix Figures A1–A5 contain training curves, but their exact values are not stated in the text.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.

Language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language-model exceptions. The supplied text does not establish whether Adam has equal or better training performance at the compared test-error minima.
Batch-size effects and recipes for recovering large-batch performance.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the generalization gap.

record.verdict_notes: The AdaBayes rows are excluded as proposed-method benchmarks; their cannot_determine states indicate exclusion, not unreadable numerical results. Other optimizer comparisons, test losses, and training curves are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not missing results. AdamW is experimentally compared with Adam, so decoupled weight decay should not be listed as wholly untested. The paper inherits optimized baseline settings rather than documenting a fresh, controlled tuning-budget comparison; uncertainty estimates are absent.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Language benchmarks; broader tuning; switching from Adam to SGD; decoupled weight decay as a recovery; word-level language models.
Batch-size comparisons and fixed-epoch batch-size effects.
Sharpness and other measures of the training-test gap.
Removal of memorized examples and its effect on test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Adam versus SGD on ResNet-34 and DenseNet-121, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, using inherited optimized baseline hyperparameters.
relationships.reason: Adam's minimum test errors exceed SGD's in every setting: 7.110 versus 5.170, 6.690 versus 5.580, 27.590 versus 22.710, and 26.640 versus 21.290 percent (R1, R4, R7, R10).
relationships.display_finding: Reported minimum test error favored SGD across both architectures and datasets under inherited baseline hyperparameters, but these comparisons remain unverified.
